source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Form 4884 Section A lines 9-16 (PDF page 20 'Recipients born before 1946': public benefits in full and private benefits up to 131,794 joint; 'if the public retirement benefits are greater than the maximum amount' no additional private subtraction, so public benefits use up the private limit; PDF page 19 'Which Benefits are Taxable': older spouse's year of birth); Schedule 1 lines 14, 27, 28 (PDF pages 14, 17); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = spouse 1 Michigan public pension 45,000.00 + spouse 2 private pension 70,000.00 + spouse 2 IRA 30,000.00 + interest 8,050.00 + taxable Social Security 42,500.00 (85% of 50,000.00) = 195,550.00. Federal taxable income = 195,550.00 - federal standard deduction (31,500 + 2 x 1,600 age 65 or older = 34,700.00) = 160,850.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan: the older spouse was born 1942, so the return uses Section A for both spouses' benefits (the younger spouse, born 1947, alone would be in the 1946-1966 branch). Section A: line 9 limit 131,794.00; line 10 military/railroad 0.00; public benefits 45,000.00 subtracted in full; private room 131,794.00 - 45,000.00 = 86,794.00; private benefits 70,000.00 + 30,000.00 = 100,000.00; smaller 86,794.00; line 16 = 45,000.00 + 86,794.00 = 131,794.00 to Schedule 1 line 27 (public and private are claimed together in Section A, not one or the other). Line 14 Social Security 42,500.00. Line 28: 29,376 - 131,794.00 < 0, so 0.00. Subtractions 174,294.00. Line 14 = 195,550.00 - 174,294.00 = 21,256.00; exemptions 2 x 5,800 = 11,600.00; line 16 = 9,656.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 9,656.00 x 0.0425 = 410.38. No credits; state income tax 410.38.
